Statement I: Article 370 conferred a special autonomous status on Jammu and Kashmir, allowing it to have its own State Constitution.
Statement II: All provisions of the Union and Concurrent Lists applied automatically to Jammu and Kashmir without concurrence of the State Government.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Validates both statements as accurate NCERT facts.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Rejected valid NCERT facts erroneously.

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to recognize error in Statement II.

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to recognize error in Statement I.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Statement I is correct: Article 370 provided special status and permitted J&K to have its own constitution. Statement II is incorrect: Union laws required state government concurrence or approval before application.
Hence Option C is correct.
Hence, option (A) is correct.

3. (C) Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh granted full statehood: February 1987.

Correct chronological sequence: (A), (B), (C), (D).
Hence, option (A) is correct.

questionText: Who was the first and only elected Sadr-i-Riyasat (Head of State) of Jammu and Kashmir before the title was changed to Governor in 1965?

options.text: Dr. Karan Singh

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Sadr-i-Riyasat Karan Singh (Regional Aspirations and Conflicts):
Dr. Karan Singh served as Regent from 1949 and then as elected Sadr-i-Riyasat from 1952 until 1965 when the post was redesignated as Governor.
Hence Option B is correct.

Therefore, option (A) is the correct answer.

questionText:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The Assam Accord established 25 March 1971 as the cutoff date for detecting and deporting illegal foreigners.
Statement II: AASU demanded that all migrants entering Assam after 1947 should immediately receive Indian citizenship.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT concept for Assam Movement Migrant Cutoff.

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Regional Aspirations and Conflicts (Assam Movement Migrant Cutoff):
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

Detailed Context:
Statement I is correct: The Assam Accord identified 25 March 1971 as the cutoff date. Statement II is incorrect: AASU demanded detection and deportation of illegal post-1951/post-1961 foreigners, not immediate blanket citizenship.
Hence Option B is correct.

Therefore, option (C) is the correct answer.
